fixes.explanation: That's it, baker! Jonah 1:17 says the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. I think that's a strange kind of help. But it's the one the text gives.

Nice thinking, friend, but that's not the one in this verse. Jonah 1:17 says the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. That's the thing He appointed here. This story isn't over, so keep your oven mitts on.
Good guess at something the LORD might appoint, friend. But Jonah 1:17 says He appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah. That's the answer for this verse. The story isn't over, so keep baking.

Seven days? Friend, that's a whole week, and the text doesn't give Jonah that much. It says he spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish. Three days in there and I'd be hunting for a customer service number.

Forty days and forty nights does show up in the Bible, when the rain fell on the earth (Genesis 7:12). I see why it came to mind. But here the text says Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish. Forty would be a very different story, friend.
The king of Nineveh isn't who Jonah names, friend. In his prayer he says to the LORD, “For You cast me into the deep…” That's who he names. The answer is right there in the prayer.
Nailed it, baker. Jonah says, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’ Notice that little word “yet.” Even with all that, he says what he will do.
That's what most of us would say, friend. But Jonah doesn't mention a swimming plan. He says, ‘…yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’ That's the thing he says he will do.
Waiting in silence makes sense, baker. But that's not what Jonah says. In his prayer he says he will look once more toward God's holy temple. That's the thing he says he will do.

Blamed? Friend, if I got swallowed by a fish I'd have a whole list of people to blame, starting with me. But Jonah says, “As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD.” Remembered is the word, and then his prayer went up to the LORD's holy temple.

Doubt would've been my first move, baker. I doubt my own oven timer on a good day. But Jonah says, “As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD.” Then his prayer went up to the LORD's holy temple.
